title: NetSuite AI: What It Is and How to Add AI Agents to NetSuite
summary: NetSuite AI spans Oracle's native features and the AI agents that run finance workflows on top of NetSuite. What it includes, what it does, and how agents extend it.
body_markdown:
NetSuite is the system of record for tens of thousands of finance teams, so "how do I add AI to NetSuite" has become one of the most common questions in corporate finance. **NetSuite AI** actually covers two different things: the AI features Oracle builds into NetSuite itself, and the AI agents that work on top of NetSuite to run finance workflows. This guide explains both, what each does for finance, and how AI agents extend NetSuite across the close, reconciliation, and reporting.


## **What is NetSuite AI?**


NetSuite AI refers to artificial intelligence applied to the NetSuite ERP, in two forms. The first is Oracle's native AI, features built directly into NetSuite (such as AI-assisted data entry, anomaly flags, and generative text). The second, and often more powerful for finance, is an AI agent layer that connects to NetSuite and runs finance work across it and your other systems. The two are complementary: native features speed up tasks inside NetSuite, while agents execute entire workflows.


> There are two ways to get AI in NetSuite: the features Oracle builds in, and the agents you connect on top. The first makes NetSuite a bit smarter; the second makes NetSuite do the work.


## **NetSuite's native AI features**


Oracle has been adding AI capabilities into NetSuite, broadly including:


- **AI-assisted data entry and coding.** Suggesting field values and GL codes to speed up transaction entry.
- **Anomaly and exception flagging.** Surfacing transactions that look unusual.
- **Generative text.** Drafting descriptions, summaries, and communications inside NetSuite.
- **Analytics assistance.** Helping users query and interpret NetSuite data.


These are useful, but they live inside NetSuite's walls and assist a human doing the work rather than running the workflow end to end.


## **The AI agent layer on top of NetSuite**


The bigger shift is connecting AI agents to NetSuite that actually do the finance work. Because finance work spans more than the ERP, it touches banking data, billing, the data warehouse, and spreadsheets, an agent layer that works across all of them can run complete workflows that native ERP features cannot:


- **Reconciliation.** Agents reconcile NetSuite balances to banks and subledgers, matching and investigating exceptions. See[AI reconciliation](https://www.concourse.ai/insights/ai-reconciliation) and NetSuite account reconciliation below.
- **The close.** Agents draft entries, run the close checklist, and flag what needs review.
- **Reporting.** Agents pull from NetSuite and assemble management and board reporting on a schedule.
- **Forecasting and analysis.** Agents build forecasts and run variance analysis from live NetSuite data.


## **NetSuite account reconciliation with AI**


Account reconciliation is one of the highest-value places to apply AI in NetSuite. Instead of exporting NetSuite balances and matching them against bank and subledger data by hand, an AI agent connects directly to NetSuite, pulls the balances, matches transactions (including imperfect, equivalent records), investigates discrepancies, and drafts the adjusting entries, with every match traceable back to the NetSuite source. That turns reconciliation from a manual, end-of-period slog into a continuous, supervised workflow.

## **Frequently asked questions**

### **Does NetSuite have built-in AI?**


Yes. Oracle has added AI features to NetSuite, including AI-assisted data entry and coding, anomaly flagging, generative text, and analytics assistance. These assist users working inside NetSuite, as distinct from AI agents that run entire workflows across NetSuite and other systems.

An AI agent can connect to NetSuite, pull balances, match them against bank and subledger data (including imperfect records), investigate discrepancies, and draft adjusting entries, with every match traceable back to the NetSuite source, turning reconciliation into a continuous, supervised workflow.


## **The bottom line**


NetSuite AI means two things: the AI features Oracle builds into NetSuite, which make working inside the ERP faster, and the AI agents you connect on top, which actually run the finance work. For finance teams on NetSuite, the biggest gains come from the agent layer, reconciliation, the close, forecasting, and reporting, that works across NetSuite and the rest of the stack, with everything traceable.
